title: When short loans pay more than long ones
hook: Would you accept less to lend your money for longer? Sometimes the market does.
metaphor: Normally a ten-year loan pays more than a three-month one, because waiting is riskier. When that flips, the machine is running backwards.
body: Lending longer should pay more. That is the normal shape.
Sometimes short loans pay more instead. This is called an inversion.
It means investors expect rates to be much lower in future.
They expect that because they expect the economy to weaken.

caveat: A warning light, not a stopwatch. There are only about 12 past episodes, and the lag has run from months to nearly two years.
